content.comment_body: Hello everyone, This is my first project using [product_name] software. My project isn't being downloaded to the device when I use Ctrl+D. The Info window only shows a PC-to-device connection and time, but the project doesn't appear on the device. I am able to ping the device and interface tests report a stable connection (green status). Could there be an issue because I am using [product_name] [version_no] while the device firmware is [version_no]? Any help would be appreciated. How can I resolve this? Thanks in advance.

To address this, you first need to identify exactly which [product_name] device you have. If it's a newer model, it may be [product_name] [version_no]. This specific hardware might not be covered in the device selection of [product_name] software version [version_no]. If your device has firmware [version_no], you need at least [product_name] software [version_no]. Preferably, use the latest version such as [version_no]. Additionally, an updated firmware is available: [version_no].
Updates can be downloaded from [url]. Please note that additional registration may be required to access these updates.
Thank you, the issue has been resolved. Using software version [version_no] allowed the project to be downloaded successfully.
Glad to hear that everything is working now.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced a version compatibility issue while transferring a project from [product_name] software [version_no] to a device with firmware [version_no]. Despite successful communications, the software was unable to download the project due to unsupported firmware. Updating to a newer [product_name] software version resolved the issue, confirming that maintaining compatibility between software and hardware versions is essential for successful project deployment.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to reliably download and implement projects from [product_name] software to the device without encountering version conflicts, especially when device communication tests indicate a proper connection.
